items.summary: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder. And there is much to behold in today's featured image. The Milky Way shines bright in the sky of Brazil, over the white sand dunes and dark lagoons of Lençóis…
items.detail: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder. And there is much to behold in today's featured image. The Milky Way shines bright in the sky of Brazil, over the white sand dunes and dark lagoons of Lençóis Maranhenses National Park. We can see different parts of the Milky Way as it apparently rotates in the sky every night and throughout the year. This composite image was taken later in the night in July from a latitude of approximately 2º south. It shows some prominent Milky Way features, such as dark dust lanes and colorful nebulas. But does the Galaxy really appear arched like a rainbow in the sky? No, this is an artifact of a picture taken with a wide-angle lens. As the Galaxy was artfully framed by the photographer, it matches the contour of the dark lagoon creating the illusion of a cosmic eye, half in space and half on the ground. Is this eye in the sky looking back at you?Tomorrow's…

items.title: 2003: Viene effettuato l'ultimo volo del Concorde.
items.summary: Viene effettuato l'ultimo volo del Concorde.
items.detail: Viene effettuato l'ultimo volo del Concorde. — L'Aérospatiale-BAC Concorde, noto semplicemente come Concorde, è stato un aereo da trasporto supersonico prodotto dal consorzio anglo-francese formato da British Aircraft Corporation (BAC) e Aérospatiale, oggi non più in servizio. Il primo volo del prototipo fu effettuato il 2 marzo 1969, mentre il 4 novembre 1970 il velivolo raggiunse per la prima volta Mach 2, diventando il secondo aereo commerciale a volare a tale velocità, dopo il sovietico Tupolev Tu-144.

items.title: This 345-million-year-old fossil had scientists fooled for decades
items.summary: A famous 345-million-year-old fossil has turned out to be something entirely different from what scientists believed for decades. Advanced X-ray imaging revealed hidden gills and thousands of tiny…
items.detail: A famous 345-million-year-old fossil has turned out to be something entirely different from what scientists believed for decades. Advanced X-ray imaging revealed hidden gills and thousands of tiny teeth, exposing a primitive aquatic or amphibious creature rather than an early reptile. The discovery suggests that several adaptations associated with life on land actually evolved in animals still dependent on water.
